page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 960 GB of system memory, providing 20 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, providing a combined total of 320 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 96293.69, placing it in the top 25 percent, while its single-core performance of 2196.39 is in the middle 50 percent. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with small-block read-only cached bandwidth reaching 7649.82 GB/sec (top 10 percent) and large-block uncached read bandwidth at 316.04 GB/sec (top 25 percent). In cryptographic and instruction-set benchmarks, the PassMark CPU extended instructions test scored 117918.35, placing it in the top 10 percent. Large-scale data decompression is also notable, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 615.79 GB/sec.

For AI workloads, the server demonstrates high throughput, processing 10308.98 tokens per second for prompt processing and 377.14 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, isolated CPU performance, though the massive GPU resources mitigate this for accelerator-bound tasks. This server is structured for deep learning, large language model inference, parallel scientific computing, and high-density memory-bound database operations.
